findings.finding: Files refresh starts loadFolder/openFile without awaiting them, then clears stale and loading. Changed or unknown file bodies and directory listings remain visible while replacement reads are pending, but the footer reports Current. Deleted selected files also retain filePreview after validation removes their cache cell; the failed reread retains the deleted preview (lines 328-330).
findings.requiredChange: Track freshness for displayed folders and previews. Keep affected bodies stale until replacement succeeds. Clear removed previews/listings when validation reports removal.
findings.requirement: On connection or refresh, show cached data as stale until validation succeeds.
findings.validation: Delay changed file/directory reads during refresh and verify stale presentation. Delete the selected file and verify its preview disappears without a late response restoring it.

findings.finding: Each panel view creates its own QueryClient (main.js:36), but every client overwrites the same persistent storage key with only its own cells. Concurrent Files and Tracker clients created before either loads data erase each other's disk results on each persist. Reloading then loses unrelated warm bodies even when storage limits are not reached.
findings.requiredChange: Coordinate persistent storage across clients, using shared ownership or isolated namespaces with bounded eviction. Do not replace another live client's unrelated entries.
findings.requirement: Refresh changed and unknown results plus their affected dependent results. Preserve unrelated current results.
findings.validation: Create two clients against one storage backend before reads. Read a file with one and a tracker tree with the other. Recreate both clients and verify both bodies survive and validate without body retransfers.

result.summary: Two specification gaps: Files freshness/removal presentation and cross-view persistent-cache overwrite. Read-only source review against 9345684e7b4a20db7ed5a0059376c5e40e1e29ed, including working changes and new cache files. No builds, tests, formatters, source edits, tracker changes, or formal receipts. Canonical replay and byte/identity hashing were treated as intentional.
